# 1.2.66 - the incident, from its opening roll to its close

The tenth and eleventh stages on the way to 1.3.0, released together. The
first (E32) writes down what an incident must hold at every step - who is in
it, what each browser is told, what breaks, who becomes a Blackened - as a grid
of 49 played-through cases that runs in every suite. The second (E07) makes the
incident hold it: one incident at a time, a fight whose turns, weapons, tools,
betrayals and Rerolls follow the rules the handbooks state, and the statistic
of every roll with a choice in it picked by the GM.

## Before installing

1. **Copy the world** (Foundry's backup of the world in Setup, or a copy of the
   world's folder). The first load moves a running incident's fight out of the
   world's data, and a copy is the only way back to it.
2. **If you can, close a running incident first.** The update carries one over
   (measured in the headless harness only; at a real table it is the live check
   LIVE-E32-02).

## After the first load, as the GM

- **Set a statistic on every project that has none.** A project's roll now
  rolls the project's own statistic, and the project editor no longer saves a
  project without one. A project made earlier without one asks a GM once, on
  its first roll, through a card in the roller's thread, and keeps the answer.
- **You pick the statistic of the incident's rolls.** A crisis action that
  lists several statistics, both openings ("Body or Hand", "Eye or Head") and
  Stage 6's clean-up rolls no longer roll the first one listed: a GM picks, on
  a card in the player's messenger thread, or in the murder window for the
  opening. A player with Resolve armed picks their own crisis action's. The
  roll waits for the pick.

## The migration

A moment after the first load of 1.2.66, the primary GM's browser runs one
step, once: **the incident's fight leaves the world's data.** The round, whose
side acts, the hindrances, what is spent and the rest of a running fight go
into the GMs' store and each participant's own copy, and leave the world's data
only once the store reads back holding them; with no incident running, what an
old one left there is dropped. A step that did not do what it should leaves the
world as it was and a notice that stays on screen, and the next load tries
again.

A GM who is not the primary and runs the migration by hand
(`game.drpg.migrate1_2_0()`) now gets a notice that nothing was marked as
migrated, and the primary GM's browser runs it when it loads the world.

## Do not go back to 1.2.65

Read in the code, not tried on a 1.2.65 build. 1.2.65 reads the fight of an
incident from the world's data, which 1.2.66 has emptied: an incident running
across a downgrade loses its round, its turn and the rest of its fight.

## Changed

- **One incident at a time.** A new incident starts from nothing left over by
  the last; no murder opens while one runs, Stage 6 included. A betrayal
  closes the first incident's Stage 6 before its own opens.
- **The betrayal.** Declared in an Eclipse it costs an action and opens when
  the Eclipse ends; none opens in a Class Trial, where the tile is dark and the
  offer stands after it. Only a body makes a Blackened or a betrayal: a Survive,
  an escape or a trap moved to Stage 6 with nobody dead records no Blackened and
  offers nothing, and everyone in the incident is told it is over.
- **A crisis action that killed cannot be rerolled**; the death stands. The
  Reroll is refused before anything is paid.
- **The opening roll carries its Night die**: at Night the killer of a direct
  murder rolls with advantage and a trap's victim with disadvantage, as the
  handbooks say. Until now the die was set and never reached the roll.
- **The hidden stash's penalty is a disadvantage die again**, as until 1.2.64,
  taken on the dice after the roll, so the roll window still does not show it.
- **Search rolls Eye**, and a project's roll and a sabotage of it the
  project's own statistic.
- **Hits.** A hit takes Sanity first and what Sanity cannot take from Health,
  and its line says what landed: the victim reads "You lose 2 Health.", everyone
  else the victim's name.
- **Weapons and tools.** The GM wears the weapon after the blow it dealt, so a
  Tier 1 knife that breaks on a Despair hit still deals its damage. The close
  breaks the weapons every killer swung, and only once Stage 6 ran; the
  discovery of a body breaks the cleaning tools its clean-up wore, even put
  away. After a critical Finishing blow the striker's first clean-up attempt
  costs no Sanity.
- **Turns.** A trap's victim acts turn after turn with no Pass; a dead killer
  takes no turn, and with none left the GMs are told and the primary GM is
  offered the close. Pin and Keep your distance last two of their side's
  turns. A victim who dies from the Students list in the fight offers Stage 6.
- **The third.** A third who averts their eyes, or fails an escape, leaves and
  stays out, and a failed escape's card says the third left. Use an item is
  not a third's. Role reversal is not open in a trap or against two killers,
  and only Role reversal heals.
- **One menu, one roll.** A crisis action's row unfolds what it costs, which
  statistics it rolls and who picks, and what a miss does; "Roll it" is the
  default, and a free take shows no threshold. The fight's tile reads "Crisis
  actions" or "Fight back", dimmed with a line while it is the other side's
  turn. The opening's request card goes when the opening does.
- **The murder window** opens on a trap's victim, says when the named killer is
  not among the living and when the killer and the victim stand in different
  rooms, and takes the opening's statistic.
- **The GM's tracker** says whose opening roll it waits for, lists the fight's
  last three turns, and a failed opening says so on screen.
- **What each browser holds.** The world's data says only whether an incident
  runs and its stage; the fight goes to the GMs and to its participants'
  browsers, each copy with what is that participant's, and who left is the
  GMs' alone.

## Known gaps

- After a Reroll, the first throw's wear notice stays in the chat.
- Two GMs: the incident's writes queue in each browser, not across them; a
  Pass or a Close on the second GM while the primary resolves an action is not
  measured (LIVE-E07-10).

## Checked

- The headless suite: 631 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped, 0 red. New in the
  suite: R205 to R214, and the incident's grid in tier 2: first run on
  1.2.65's code, 28 of its then 46 cases were red; all 49 are green now. The
  seventeen scenarios end green: 13-murder-signals 69/69, the new
  19-standing-cast 8/8, the security scenario 106/106, 40-flow 59/59,
  61-gmstore-case 93/93, and 72-canary 82/85 and 11-killer-secrecy 13/14,
  their reds each a later stage's or a Foundry limit.
- An independent review in two rounds (security, and whether the change is
  correct and its tests measure); its findings were fixed in ten commits.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet, and listed in the audit's live checks
  (LIVE-E32-01 and 02, LIVE-E07-01 to 12): the grid on a real world and an
  incident carried across the update; the fight from the Eclipse to Stage 6 on
  three accounts, the betrayal, the Despair knife, the damage lines, the menu
  and Daggerheart's roll window with the GM's pick, a trap's turns, the tools
  at the discovery, the murder window on a Polish client, the tracker, two GMs,
  the wait for the GM's pick at a table, and the Night die's chip in the
  opening's roll window. The local release gate needs a local Foundry v14 and
  did not run for this release.
